# 1.2.115 - the case's copy on the server for every GM, a masked killer hidden from everyone not in on it, an Event panel that never scrolls, the six statistics in one row and the Interface scale down to 25 %

Four stages and three lines of work on 1.2.114 (9e7e3d78, tag v1.2.114): E56's second part (comments and dead code),
E109 (the owner's answers on the review page DRPG-Q113 and 1.2.113's leftovers), E59 (each mechanic's chain held to
the code, the handbooks and the texts) and E111 (the case's copy on the server, and Clear the plan); and, outside the
stages, the tooltip sweep, the six statistics' row with the Interface scale, and three bugs the owner reported from a
real table on 1.2.114. The owner's rule of 14.11.2026, written into tools/stages.json on 15.11: 1.2.115 closes
everything that does not need a real Foundry; E39, E40, E43, E53, E58 and E83 (the local-Foundry stages and the audit)
moved to 1.2.116, and E26 stays 1.3.0. From v1.2.114 to b07327f9, the tree before this release commit: 161 commits, 26
of them merges between the lines and the assembly (`git rev-list --count` and `--merges --count` over
v1.2.114..b07327f9).

In plain words:

**The case's copy on the server, for every GM** (E111; the owner, 14.11.2026: "Planer zagadki powinien przechowywac
dane w przegladarce gmow i byc wspolny dla kazdego gma", then "Bez hasel prosze - niech to bedzie dostepne dla kont
gmow po prostu").
- **A GM who opens the world alone on another computer finds the case there.** Until now the case lived only in the
  GMs' browsers, which bring each other up to date only while two of them are online together. Now the primary GM's
  browser also keeps the whole case - what **Back up** saves - in a file on the Foundry server:
  `worlds/<world>/drpg-case/case-<32 hex digits>.json`, about 15 seconds after the case changes and at most a minute
  after the first change (case-copy.mjs `SEAL_QUIET_MS`, `SEAL_MOST_MS`). Every GM's browser reads it when it opens
  the world and merges it as **Restore from a file** does.
- **An empty browser never replaces a full copy**: every write first lists the folder and merges every copy in it, and
  no browser writes before its stores have heard the other GMs. Two GMs' first writes that race leave two files; both
  are read, and the newer is written on from then on.
- **What protects it is not encryption.** It is two things, both Foundry's: only an account that may browse files can
  list the folder, which the module keeps off the Player and Trusted Player roles (the setting **Keep players out of
  the file browser**), and the file's name is 128 random bits that nothing a player's browser receives contains.
  Foundry's server hands a file of the data folder to anyone who asks for its exact address, logged in or not
  (assumed, not measured: LIVE-E111-02), so a name that leaks gives the whole case away. The module therefore writes
  no copy while that setting is off, or while a Player, a Trusted Player or a player's own account may browse or
  upload files; it tells the GMs why, and the health check names it.
- **The Case window shows the copy**: when it was last written and by whom, and **Write the copy now**.
- A first design with a GM passphrase and an encrypted copy in a world setting was built and taken out whole before
  this release, on the owner's word above.

**Clear the plan** (E111; the owner, 14.11.2026: "Brakuje mi tez w planerze zagadki opcji zresetowania
zawartosci/wyczyszczenia recznie.").
- A button in the Investigation window's footer, in both its views, clears one chapter's plan: its planned Key
  Remnants, its case schema's nodes and the schema's layout. The chapter is picked first (the clock's chapter by
  default), and a question counts what goes and names the Key Remnants already placed, whose Remnants stay on the map.
- Remnants, Truth Bullets, the nodes ticked in the Class Trial and other chapters' plans stay. The plan goes on every
  GM's browser and in the server copy, and a GM who was away does not bring it back. Any GM, an Assistant too; never a
  player. It cannot be undone.

**A killer behind a "?" is "?" to everyone not in on it** (the owner, from a table on 1.2.114: "Tozsamosc mordercy
przy odpowiednim rzucie powinna byc tajna tez dla osob postronnych, tak samo jak dla ofiary").
- **In the fight**: the crisis card's heading, its loss lines and the opening card name the killer only to the GMs and
  the players of the killer and any accomplice, and "?" to the victim and every bystander; a drawn roll's and a
  Reroll's dice reach the others with no roller and no portrait, so Dice So Nice throws them as the message's author,
  a GM; Listen's lines from next door, and their Reroll, say "?" for a masked character. Before the fix, the victim's
  browser held the killer's name on the cards, the notices and the history, and the killer's player on the dice
  (scenario 21, measured on the assembly at e0ee06ef).
- **Outside the fight, while the mask stands** (the mask outlives the incident): the six player pickers that list the
  people in a room (Palm, Tail, Tamper's frame, a handover, a Call's room picker, a Monocub's targets) and the Frisk's
  ask show "?"; every private card's words write "?" for that reader; every card is veiled and a player's card goes
  through the GM, as during an incident. The token's dynamic ring picture is masked and put back as well.
- Still Foundry's limit, as before: a token keeps its actor, and every browser holds every actor, so a console still
  reaches the name.

**Characters are drawn over Remnants and traces** (the owner: "Gdy token postaci jest w tym samym miejscu co remnant,
postac zawsze niech bedzie na wierzchu").
- A Remnant's and a project token's picture now sits on its own layer just under Foundry's tokens (sort layer 699),
  under every character, Monokuma and Monocub, and still above tiles and drawings. Isometric Perspective 14.0.6 (read
  in its release, not run) rewrites every token's order by depth on the screen, so a trace on a character's spot fell
  above or below it by chance; the traces now leave its pass. Elevation is not touched.

**The Event panel never scrolls** (the owner: "Na karcie eventu nigdy nie powinno byc scrolla").
- The panel has no height cap: it is as tall as its cards, down to the screen's bottom or the module's block below it
  (the HUD, the room tile, the notices, the voice tile and the corner's buttons among them) or Foundry's hotbar, 8 px
  clear.
- Past that room, cards fold to their titles from the last up; the first card, or the one the reader opened, stays
  open. A folded card opens on a click, Enter or Space. Titles that still do not fit are counted as "+N" under the
  panel.
- Measured on 60 panels a murder puts up (5 cases, both themes, English and Polish, three screen sizes;
  audit/events-murder-fit.mjs): all 60 scrolled before (at e0ee06ef), none after.

**The six statistics in one row** (the owner, 14.11.2026, on an 850 px sheet under Stained Glass: "Podoba mi sie
pomysl by wysrodkowac, ale koniecznie w 1 rzedzie").
- The row is six equal columns, each statistic centred. Where it does not fit, it gives way in steps and keeps the
  first that fits: the gap, the plate's padding, the names' letter-spacing, the mark above the name, then
  Daggerheart's short names (LEG BOD HAN EYE SHA HEA) with the full name as the plate's tooltip. Three over three is
  left only for a row under about 322 px at 100 % (measured in Chromium on Daggerheart 2.12.8's stylesheet built from
  its source, not in Foundry).

**The Interface scale down to 25 %** (the owner: "Chcialbym powiekszyc tez zakres zmniejszenia ui (aktualnie minimum
to 0.8, celujmy w 0.25").
- The slider goes from 25 % to 140 % (it was 80 %). From 80 % up nothing changes. Under 80 % the readability floor
  follows the slider, so words and boxes shrink together; a line under the slider says the text is then smaller than
  the module's readable size. A window's header buttons keep a 24 px target under 80 %.
- At 25 %, fixed where they broke: the compact voice tile (its buttons stood outside it), the sheet's left column (the
  sheet scrolled sideways) and the room tile (its toggle and pips lay over the name).

## Before installing

- **No world migration.** No setting is added or removed: `game.settings.register` appears on 198 lines of scripts/ at
  both ends, and settings.mjs's code changes only the Interface scale's range. The GMs' stores are the same 64
  definitions with the same keys (gm-stores.mjs; gm-store.mjs has no change), so their client settings read as before.
- **New stored data: one file on the server.** Once a GM's browser has heard the other GMs, it reads
  `worlds/<world>/drpg-case/`, and the primary GM's browser creates the folder and writes `case-<32 hex>.json` about
  15 seconds later - only while **Keep players out of the file browser** is on and no Player, Trusted Player or
  player's account may browse or upload files; otherwise it writes nothing and the primary GM is told why. The file is
  not encrypted: its protection is the unguessable name plus Foundry's file permissions. The module never deletes a
  copy (Foundry's FilePicker has no delete); a GM removes an old one by hand. Hosts whose file source is not "data"
  (The Forge, S3) are not modelled (LIVE-E111-01).
- **Language**: lang/en.json goes from 6077 to 6335 keys: 258 added (208 of them the sweep's tooltips), none removed,
  64 changed in wording (counted on the flattened files, v1.2.114 against 5993538b: a key added is in the new file
  only, a key changed has a different value). lang/pl.json holds every English key and no other key but the Polish
  plural forms (.few, .many; 532, 10 new for the new plural keys) and the 553 DRPG.Config.* keys it held before (same
  count).
- **The Interface scale**: a stored value from 80 % up reads as before; the slider now reaches 25 %.
- **With Isometric Perspective**: the traces leave its depth sort, so a floor trace in front of a wall tile it lifts
  to the tokens' layer is drawn under that tile (Q-OWN115-4, below).
- **While a mask stands**, every player's private card is posted through a GM, as during an incident, and waits for a
  GM to be connected (Q-OWN115-8).
- **Daggerheart**: `verified` stays 2.12.8, the newest version run at a table. 2.12.9 came out on 14.11.2026; its
  release notes name adversary types, action ranges, a grouped action's button and compendium texts, none of them
  rolls, Hope and Fear, chat, tokens or settings (read, not run). The module warns the GM once on a newer version.
- Two icons are added (icons/remnant-facility.svg, icons/remnant-infiltrate.svg). No console name changed
  (tools/api-surface.json has no change in the range).
